definition_zh: 电路；环行路线；巡回
definition_en: a complete path through which electric current flows, a route that returns to its start, or a regular round of visits
core_image: 电流沿着一圈导线跑回起点
scene: 桌上摊着一块电路板，指示灯一闪一闪。A loose wire broke the circuit.
sceneCN: 这里 circuit 指「电路」（第 1 个义项：电流可以流过的闭合路径）；句意是一根松脱的导线让电路断开了。

senses.title: A closed path for current
senses.definition: a complete path through which electric current can flow
senses.definitionCN: 电流可以流过的完整路径
senses.example: A loose wire broke the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 一根松脱的导线让电路断开了。
senses.why: Latin circuitus meant a going around, and electricity repeats that closed loop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circuitus 意为绕行，电流重复的正是这种闭合环路。

senses.title: A circular route
senses.definition: a route that goes around and comes back to the start
senses.definitionCN: 绕一圈后回到起点的路线
senses.example: The race covers a five kilometre circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛跑一圈五公里的环道。
senses.why: The going-around sense named any path that returns on itself.
senses.whyCN: 绕行的意思用来指任何自身闭合的路线。

senses.title: A regular round of visits
senses.definition: a regular series of visits to several places in turn
senses.definitionCN: 依次到多个地点的一轮例行访问
senses.example: The judge travels a country circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 这位法官在乡间巡回审案。
senses.why: Officials who rode from town to town completed a ring of visits.
senses.whyCN: 官员从一镇走到另一镇，正好走完一圈行程。

intro.en: Circuit is Latin for a going around, built from around plus to go.
intro.cn: circuit 在拉丁语中意为绕行，由「周围」与「走」两部分构成。

items.en: Circum meant around on every side.
items.cn: circum 意为四周环绕。

items.en: Ire meant to go.
items.cn: ire 意为走。

items.en: Circuitus named the act of going round.
items.cn: circuitus 指绕行这一动作。

items.en: Circuit kept the legal and travelling senses.
items.cn: circuit 保留了法律与巡行的意思。

items.en: English used circuit for a judge's round of towns.
items.cn: 英语用 circuit 指法官巡视各镇的行程。

items.en: Electricity gave the word its most familiar sense.
items.cn: 电学赋予这个词最熟悉的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ring root, while the meaning group names paths and routes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语圆环词根，近义组列出路径与路线。

entries.definition: a round closed shape
shaped like a circle
a show performed in a ring
entries.definitionCN: 在圆环场地演出的表演

entries.definition: a path that returns to itself
a way from one place to another
a line along which something moves

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin parts, the electric loop and the judge's round.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用两个拉丁语部件、电流环路以及法官巡行。

normal.en: Split circuit into circu and it: a ring plus a going, so a going round.
normal.cn: 把 circuit 拆成 circu 与 it：一个圈加一次走，就是绕一圈。

normal.en: A broken circuit stops the current because the ring is no longer closed.
normal.cn: 电路断了电流就停，因为那个环不再闭合。

normal.en: Short circuit skips the long path, and short-circuit as a verb means to bypass.
normal.cn: 短路跳过了长路径，动词 short-circuit 便表示绕过。

normal.en: The racing circuit is a loop of road, and the lecture circuit is a loop of towns.
normal.cn: 赛车环道是一圈路，巡回讲学是一圈城镇。

normal.en: Circuitous keeps the going-around idea in adjective form.
normal.cn: circuitous 以形容词形式保留绕行的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire returning to the battery it left.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细导线回到它出发的那块电池。

abstract.en: Picture a car passing the same grandstand again.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车再次经过同一座看台。

abstract.en: Picture a judge's carriage stopping in one more market square.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的马车又在另一个集市广场停下。

examples.en: Water got into the circuit and stopped the machine.
examples.cn: 水进了电路，机器停了下来。

examples.en: They drove one full circuit of the park.
examples.cn: 他们绕公园整整开了一圈。

examples.en: The band spent the summer on the festival circuit.
examples.cn: 乐队整个夏天都在音乐节巡回演出。

dict_mnemonic.text: circuit 拆成 circu 与 it：绕一圈，再走回来。

root: 源自拉丁语 circuitus（绕行），由 circum（周围）与 ire（走）构成，本指走一圈回到原处。

sensesIntro.en: A going around gives the closed path, then any returning route, and then a round of official visits.
sensesIntro.cn: 绕行先给出闭合路径，再给出任何回到原处的路线，最后给出官员的一轮巡访。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current running a ring of wire back to its source.
core.cn: 核心意象：电流沿一圈导线跑回它的源头。

branches.en: The electric loop is the modern everyday sense.
branches.cn: 电流环路是现代最日常的义项。

branches.en: Any route that returns is a circuit of road.
branches.cn: 任何回到原处的路线都是一圈道路。

branches.en: A judge's round of towns repeats the ring on a map.
branches.cn: 法官巡行各镇，在地图上重复同一个环。

branches.en: Wire and road share one closed geometry.
branches.cn: 导线与道路共享同一个闭合几何。

branches.en: A racing loop and a lecture loop both end where they began.
branches.cn: 赛车环道与巡回讲学都在起点结束。

intro.en: The stem circuit builds a plural, two derived adjectives and a compound verb.
intro.cn: 词干 circuit 构成复数、两个派生形容词以及一个复合动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circum around plus ire to go produced circuitus, the base of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circum（周围）加 ire（走）构成 circuitus，是整个词族的词基。

items.exampleCN: 这块板上集成了三条电路。
我们走了一条绕远的路。
circum- 是 circuit 的开头。

latinEntries.example: Circuitus is the direct source of circuit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circuitus 是 circuit 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Circumire combines around with to go.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circumire 把周围与走合在一起。

definition_zh: 循环；流通；发行量
definition_en: the movement of blood around the body, the passing of money or news among people, or the number of copies of a publication sold
core_image: 报纸从印刷机上一叠叠装车送走
scene: 报摊上的报纸一早就被取空，印刷机还在转。The magazine has a circulation of half a million.
sceneCN: 这里 circulation 指「发行量」（第 3 个义项：报刊每期售出的份数）；句意是这本杂志的发行量有五十万份。

senses.title: Movement of blood
senses.definition: the movement of blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 血液在全身的流动
senses.example: Exercise improves the circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 运动能改善血液循环。
senses.why: Latin circulatio named the act of moving in a ring, and blood was the first thing described.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circulatio 指沿环移动，血液是最早被描述的对象。

senses.title: Passing among people
senses.definition: the passing of money, goods or news among people
senses.definitionCN: 货币、货物或消息在人群中的流转
senses.example: New coins are now in circulation.
senses.exampleCN: 新硬币现在已在流通。
senses.why: Money and news follow the same loop as blood in a body.
senses.whyCN: 货币与消息遵循的正是血液在体内那样的环路。

senses.title: Copies sold or sent out
senses.definition: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine sold
senses.definitionCN: 报刊每期售出的份数
senses.example: The magazine has a circulation of half a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志的发行量有五十万份。
senses.why: The number of copies sent round measures how far the paper travels.
senses.whyCN: 绕着送出的份数，衡量的就是这份报纸走得有多远。

intro.en: Circulation is the Latin noun of action for moving in a ring.
intro.cn: circulation 是表示沿环移动的拉丁语动作名词。

items.en: Circulus named a small ring.
items.cn: circulus 指小圆环。

items.en: Circulare meant to move something round.
items.cn: circulare 意为使某物绕行。

items.en: Circulatio named the act of going round.
items.cn: circulatio 指绕行的动作。

items.en: English circulation first described the blood.
items.cn: 英语 circulation 最初描述血液的流动。

items.en: The word extended to money, news and printed copies.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到货币、消息与印刷份数。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ring root, while the meaning group names flows and reach.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语圆环词根，近义组列出流动与覆盖范围。

entries.definition: a round closed shape
shaped like a circle
a closed path for electric current
a steady movement of liquid or air
entries.definitionCN: 液体或空气平稳的流动

entries.definition: the act of giving out to many people
the people who read a publication
entries.definitionCN: 阅读某份出版物的人群

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ion noun ending, the blood image and the newspaper number.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 -ion 名词词尾、血液意象以及报刊份数。

normal.en: Circulation is the noun of circulate, so the ending -ion marks the act.
normal.cn: circulation 是 circulate 的名词，-ion 词尾标记动作。

normal.en: Blood circulation, money circulation, newspaper circulation: three loops of different size.
normal.cn: blood circulation、money circulation、newspaper circulation，三个大小不同的环。

normal.en: In circulation means out among people, not locked in a drawer.
normal.cn: in circulation 指在人群里流转，而不是锁在抽屉里。

normal.en: A magazine with a large circulation reaches many hands each month.
normal.cn: 发行量大的杂志每个月能到许多人手里。

normal.en: Withdraw from circulation is the opposite path, taking money or goods out of the loop.
normal.cn: withdraw from circulation 是相反的路径，把钱或货从环里取出。

abstract.en: Picture a warm pulse moving from the wrist up the arm.
abstract.cn: 想象温热的脉搏从手腕一路向上走。

abstract.en: Picture a coin passing through five hands in one day.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币一天里经过五个人的手。

abstract.en: Picture stacked papers sliding into a delivery van.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠叠报纸滑进送货车里。

examples.en: Cold hands are a sign of poor circulation.
examples.cn: 手发凉是循环不好的迹象。

examples.en: The old notes were taken out of circulation.
examples.cn: 旧纸币被停止流通。

examples.en: The paper doubled its circulation in one year.
examples.cn: 这家报纸一年内发行量翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: circulation 与 circulate 同根：绕一圈送出的份数，就是发行量。

root: 源自拉丁语 circulatio（绕行），由 circulare（使成环）派生，本指沿环流动，后指报刊绕送的份数。

sensesIntro.en: The act of moving in a ring starts with blood, then covers money and news, and finally counts the copies sent out.
sensesIntro.cn: 沿环移动先落在血液上，再覆盖货币与消息，最后用来数绕着送出的份数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: printed sheets leaving the press in tight stacks.
core.cn: 核心意象：印好的纸一叠叠离开印刷机。

branches.en: Blood is the first and most physical sense.
branches.cn: 血液是最早也最具体的义项。

branches.en: Money and news repeat the bodily loop in society.
branches.cn: 货币与消息在社会中重复身体里的环。

branches.en: The count of copies measures the width of the loop.
branches.cn: 份数衡量的是这个环有多宽。

branches.en: Body and economy share one noun of continuous flow.
branches.cn: 身体与经济共用一个表示持续流动的名词。

branches.en: A paper in circulation earns its circulation figure.
branches.cn: 在流通中的报纸才挣得它的发行量数字。

intro.en: The noun stem builds a plural, an adjective and the verb it comes from.
intro.cn: 这个名词词干构成复数、一个形容词以及它由之而来的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circulatio grows from circulare, and -ion marks the resulting action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circulatio 由 circulare 长出，-ion 标记由此形成的动作名词。

items.example: The two papers report different circulations.
items.exampleCN: 两家报纸公布的发行量不同。

items.example: Air must circulate behind the fridge.
The tank has a circular base.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子有一个圆形底座。

items.example: The circle is drawn in chalk.

latinEntries.example: Circulatio is the direct source of circulation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circulatio 是 circulation 的直接来源。

definition_zh: n. 圆周；周长；（绕圆一周的）周边
definition_en: the line that goes round a circle, or the distance around it
core_image: 一条沿着圆形边缘绕行一周的线
scene: 她沿着跑道走完一整圈，算出操场周长为四百米。She walked the track once to measure its circumference.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：circumference 指圆周或周长；句意是她沿着跑道走完一整圈，算出操场周长为四百米。

senses.title: The boundary line of a circle
senses.definition: the continuous line that forms the edge of a circle
senses.definitionCN: 构成圆形边缘的连续曲线
senses.example: The fence follows the circumference of the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 篱笆沿着池塘的圆周延伸。
senses.why: Latin circum means around and ferre means to carry.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circum 意为环绕，ferre 意为携带。

senses.title: The distance around a circle
senses.definition: the measured length of the line around a circle
senses.definitionCN: 绕圆一周所量得的长度
senses.example: Her waist circumference fell by two inches.
senses.exampleCN: 她的腰围减了两英寸。
senses.why: A drawn line became a number you can measure.
senses.whyCN: 画出的线变成可以测量的数值。

intro.en: Circumference joins a Latin prefix of circling to a Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: circumference 由表示环绕的拉丁前缀和表示携带的拉丁动词组成。

items.en: Circum means around or on all sides.
items.cn: circum 意为环绕、四周。

items.en: Ferre means to carry or bear.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带、承担。

items.en: The noun means a carrying around, a line drawn around.
items.cn: 该名词意为绕行一周、画出的环线。

items.en: English borrows the term for the edge of a circle.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入几何学指圆的边缘。

items.en: The word also names the distance measured around a body or shape.
items.cn: 现代也指绕物体量出的长度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the circum- shape; the near-meaning group names other ways round a shape.
note.cn: 形近组共享 circum- 词形；近义组列出围绕图形的其他说法。

entries.definition: To draw a line around or limit.
A line or route that goes round.
The facts around an event.
The distance round a shape.
The distance around something thick.
The line that marks a limit.

normalIntro.en: Think of a string that walks all the way around a wheel.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一根细绳绕着车轮走完一整圈。

normal.en: Circum means around.
normal.cn: circum 意为环绕。

normal.en: Fer means carry.
normal.cn: fer 意为携带。

normal.en: Carry a string around the circle.
normal.cn: 把绳子沿着圆带一圈。

normal.en: The length of that walk is the circumference.
normal.cn: 这一圈的长度就是周长。

normal.en: A waist has a circumference too.
normal.cn: 腰围也是一种周长。

abstract.en: A road that refuses to end.
abstract.cn: 一条不肯结束的路。

abstract.en: The edge of a coin laid flat.
abstract.cn: 平放硬币的边缘。

abstract.en: Distance wearing a circle as a coat.
abstract.cn: 把圆当外衣穿的距离。

examples.en: The circumference of the table is three metres.
examples.cn: 这张桌子的周长是三米。

examples.en: They planted flowers around the circumference of the lawn.
examples.cn: 他们沿着草坪四周种花。

examples.en: Doctors recorded the waist circumference of each child.
examples.cn: 医生记录了每个孩子的腰围。

dict_mnemonic.text: circum（环绕）+ fer（带）+ ence（名词）→ 带着绕一圈的长度。

root: 拉丁 circum（环绕）+ ferre（携带）→ circumferentia（绕行一周）→ 英语 circumference

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the line around a circle and the length of that line.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指圆边的线，也指这条线的长度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line travelling all the way around a circle
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕着圆走完一圈的细线

branches.en: A chalk line drawn around a coin.
branches.cn: 粉笔绕着硬币画的一圈。

branches.en: A hedge following a pond edge.
branches.cn: 沿池塘边缘的树篱。

branches.en: A tape measure around a waist.
branches.cn: 绕在腰上的软尺。

branches.en: A runner recording the distance of one lap.
branches.cn: 跑者记录一圈的距离。

branches.en: The same ring seen as line and as number.
branches.cn: 同一个环，既是线也是数。

intro.en: Circumference is built from Latin pieces; the list adds words of rings, carrying and measuring.
intro.cn: circumference 由拉丁语成分构成；下面列出圆环、携带与测量词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin circum is around, ferre is to carry, and metrum is a measure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circum 意为环绕，ferre 意为携带，metrum 意为量度。

latinEntries.exampleCN: circumferentia 产生 circumference 与 circumferential。
circus 产生 circus 与 circular。
perimetros 产生 perimeter 与 perimetric。

definition_zh: v. 限制，约束；在…周围画线；使（图形）外接
definition_en: to limit the power or activity of something; to draw a line around a shape
core_image: 用笔在纸上画一个圈，把一处地方围住
scene: 新法规限制了市政委员会的权力范围。New laws circumscribe the powers of the council.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：circumscribe 指限制；句意是新法规限制了市政委员会的权力范围。

senses.title: To draw a line around
senses.definition: to draw a line that encloses a shape or space
senses.definitionCN: 画出包围某个形状或空间的线
senses.example: The teacher circumscribed the map with red ink.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用红墨水把地图圈了起来。
senses.why: Circum means around and scribere means to write.
senses.whyCN: circum 意为环绕，scribere 意为书写。

senses.title: To limit the scope of something
senses.definition: to set limits on what someone may do or decide
senses.definitionCN: 限定某人可以做或决定的范围
senses.example: New rules circumscribe what the committee can spend.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定限制了委员会可以花多少钱。
senses.why: A boundary drawn on paper became a limit on action.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的边界变成了对行动的限制。

intro.en: The word begins as geometry and ends as a word for limits on power.
intro.cn: 这个词从几何学出发，最后指对权力的限制。

items.en: Circum means around.
items.cn: circum 意为环绕。

items.en: Scribere means to write or draw.
items.cn: scribere 意为书写、画出。

items.en: The verb means to draw a line around.
items.cn: 该动词意为在周围画线。

items.en: English uses it for a shape drawn round another.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用它指外接图形。

items.en: It now means to limit powers or choices.
items.cn: 现代指限制权力或选择。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scrib- or circum- shape; the near-meaning group names ways of limiting.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scrib- 或 circum- 词形；近义组列出限制的说法。

entries.definition: The line or distance around a circle.
To say what something is like.
To state a rule or medicine.
To keep within limits.
To keep within an area.
To set the greatest amount allowed.

normalIntro.en: Picture a writer drawing a fence line round a field.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一位书写者绕着田野画一圈围线。

normal.en: Circum is around.
normal.cn: circum 是环绕。

normal.en: Scribe is write.
normal.cn: scribe 是书写。

normal.en: Write a line around the thing.
normal.cn: 在这个东西周围画一条线。

normal.en: The line becomes a rule you cannot cross.
normal.cn: 这条线成了不能越过的规则。

normal.en: Laws circumscribe our choices.
normal.cn: 法律限定了我们的选择。

abstract.en: A pencil acting as a wall.
abstract.cn: 一支铅笔充当墙壁。

abstract.en: Freedom inside a circled field.
abstract.cn: 圈内有限度的自由。

abstract.en: Geometry turning into government.
abstract.cn: 几何变成了治理。

examples.en: The garden was circumscribed by a low stone wall.
examples.cn: 花园被一道矮石墙围了起来。

examples.en: Strict rules circumscribe how the money may be used.
examples.cn: 严格的规定限定了这笔钱的使用方式。

examples.en: The circle is circumscribed around the square.
examples.cn: 这个圆是正方形的外接圆。

dict_mnemonic.text: circum（环绕）+ scribe（写）→ 在四周写下界限，即限制。

root: 拉丁 circum（环绕）+ scribere（书写、画）→ circumscribere（画圈界定）

sensesIntro.en: A line drawn around a shape became a line drawn around a life.
sensesIntro.cn: 画在图形外的线，最终成了画在生活外的线。

core.cn: 核心意象：笔在纸上描出一个闭合的圈

branches.en: Red ink circling a map.
branches.cn: 红墨圈住地图。

branches.en: A fence drawn around a garden.
branches.cn: 花园四周画出的栅栏线。

branches.en: A rule narrowing a budget.
branches.cn: 缩小预算范围的规则。

branches.en: A law fencing in a committee.
branches.cn: 把委员会圈住的法律。

branches.en: A ring that is both drawing and decree.
branches.cn: 既是图画又是法令的圆圈。

intro.en: Circumscribe carries a prefix of circling and a root of writing; the list adds words of limits.
intro.cn: circumscribe 带有环绕前缀和书写词根；下面列出界限词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin circum is around, scribere is to write, and finis is an end.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circum 意为环绕，scribere 意为书写，finis 意为终点。

latinEntries.exampleCN: circumscribere 产生 circumscribe 与 circumscription。
scribere 产生 describe 与 prescribe。
finis 产生 confine 与 final。

definition_zh: 情况；环境；境况
definition_en: the facts and conditions that affect an event, the conditions of a person's life, or a person's financial position
core_image: 一个人站在四周密密麻麻的条件中间
scene: 雨下得很大，末班车又提前开走了。Under the circumstances, we decided to stay.
sceneCN: 这里 circumstances 指「情况」（第 1 个义项：影响某个决定的周边事实）；句意是在这种情况下，我们决定留下。

senses.title: The facts around an event
senses.definition: the facts and conditions that affect an event or a decision
senses.definitionCN: 影响某个事件或决定的周边事实与条件
senses.example: Under the circumstances, we decided to stay.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种情况下，我们决定留下。
senses.why: Latin circumstantia meant standing around, so the facts standing around an event took the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circumstantia 意为站在四周，围绕事件的事实便得了这个名字。

senses.title: Surrounding conditions
senses.definition: the conditions of life that surround a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个人或一群人的生活条件
senses.example: Children here grow up in difficult circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的孩子在艰难的环境中长大。
senses.why: What stands around a person forms the setting of a whole life.
senses.whyCN: 围绕一个人站立的东西，构成了整段生活的背景。

senses.title: Financial position
senses.definition: the level of money and comfort of a person or a family
senses.definitionCN: 个人或家庭的金钱与生活水平
senses.example: Her circumstances improved after the new job.
senses.exampleCN: 新工作之后她的境况好转了。
senses.why: Money became the measure of the ground a person stands on.
senses.whyCN: 金钱成了衡量一个人脚下立足之地的尺度。

intro.en: Circumstance is Latin for a standing around, as conditions stand around an event.
intro.cn: circumstance 在拉丁语中意为「站在四周」，正如条件围绕事件而立。

items.en: Circum meant around on every side.
items.cn: circum 意为四周环绕。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Circumstantia named the things standing around.
items.cn: circumstantia 指站在四周的事物。

items.en: Circonstance carried the word into French.
items.cn: circonstance 把这个词带进法语。

items.en: English circumstance named the setting of an act.
items.cn: 英语 circumstance 指一个行为的背景。

items.en: The plural widened to life conditions and money.
items.cn: 复数形式扩展到生活条件与金钱状况。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the circum- opening, while the meaning group names settings and conditions.
note.cn: 形近组共享 circum- 开头，近义组列出背景与条件。

entries.definition: the distance around the edge of a circle
based on indirect evidence
to find a way around a rule
the set of things happening at a time
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻发生的一整套事情

entries.definition: the state that something is in
the facts around an event or a word
entries.definitionCN: 围绕事件或词语的事实

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing-around image, the three senses and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「站在四周」的意象、三层意思以及固定搭配。

normal.en: Split circumstance into circum and stance: everything standing around you.
normal.cn: 把 circumstance 拆成 circum 与 stance：站在你四周的一切。

normal.en: Under the circumstances is the most common frame, meaning because of the facts.
normal.cn: under the circumstances 是最常见的框架，意为「鉴于这些事实」。

normal.en: Under no circumstances is a strong refusal, and it keeps the same plural shape.
normal.cn: under no circumstances 表示坚决否定，形状仍是复数。

normal.en: The plural is normal, because many conditions stand around one event.
normal.cn: 通常用复数，因为围绕一个事件的条件有很多。

normal.en: Circumstantial evidence is evidence from the things standing around a case.
normal.cn: circumstantial evidence 就是来自案件周边事物的证据。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still while rain, traffic and clock hands press in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站住不动，雨、车流与钟表的指针都压过来。

abstract.en: Picture a small family in a narrow room with one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小家庭挤在有盏灯的窄房间里。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of bills on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房桌上放着一叠账单。

examples.en: Under the circumstances, the delay was understandable.
examples.cn: 在这种情况下，延误是可以理解的。

examples.en: Many families live in hard circumstances.
examples.cn: 许多家庭生活在艰苦的环境中。

examples.en: He rose above his circumstances through study.
examples.cn: 他靠学习摆脱了自己的境况。

dict_mnemonic.text: circumstance 拆成 circum 与 stance：站在你周围的一切，就是你的处境。

root: 源自拉丁语 circumstantia（站在四周），由 circum（周围）与 stare（站立）构成，本指围绕事件的条件。

sensesIntro.en: Things standing around an act give the case facts, then the setting of a life, and finally the money a person stands on.
sensesIntro.cn: 围绕行为而立的事物先给出具体情况，再给出生活背景，最后给出一个人脚下的钱财。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in the middle of pressing conditions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在层层条件包围的中间。

branches.en: The facts of a case are the first sense.
branches.cn: 案件的具体事实是第一层意思。

branches.en: The setting of a life is the plural at work.
branches.cn: 生活背景是复数形式的常见用法。

branches.en: Money is the narrowest and most personal sense.
branches.cn: 金钱是最窄也最贴近个人的义项。

branches.en: One event and a whole life both sit inside conditions.
branches.cn: 单个事件与整段人生都坐在条件之中。

branches.en: Money decides much of the ground a family stands on.
branches.cn: 金钱决定了一个家庭脚下的大部分立足之地。

intro.en: The stem builds a plural, an adjective and an adverb from one Latin frame.
intro.cn: 这个词干在一个拉丁框架上构成复数、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circum around plus stare to stand produced circumstantia, the base of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circum（周围）加 stare（站立）构成 circumstantia，是整个词族的词基。

items.exampleCN: 当时的情况对我们不利。

items.example: The case rested on circumstantial proof.

items.exampleCN: 这一关联是以间接方式证明的。
circum- 是 circumstance 的开头。

items.example: Stance carries the sense of standing.

latinEntries.example: Circumstantia is the direct source of circumstance.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circumstantia 是 circumstance 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Circumstare joins around with to stand.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circumstare 把周围与站立合在一起。

definition_zh: n. 马戏团；马戏表演；圆形广场（多作街道名）；乱哄哄的场面
definition_en: a group that performs acrobatics and clowning in a big tent; a round open space
core_image: 圆顶帐篷里，小丑和杂技演员轮番上场
scene: 孩子们坐在大帐篷里，看小丑在圆场中央表演。The children watched the clowns perform in the centre of the circus ring.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：circus 指马戏团或马戏场；句意是孩子们坐在大帐篷里，看小丑在圆场中央表演。

senses.title: A travelling show with acrobats
senses.definition: a show of acrobatics, animals and clowns, often in a tent
senses.definitionCN: 常在帐篷里表演杂技、动物与小丑的演出
senses.example: The circus arrived with three lorries and a tall tent.
senses.exampleCN: 马戏团带着三辆卡车和一座高帐篷来了。
senses.why: Latin circus first meant a ring for races.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circus 最初指赛跑用的圆环场地。

senses.title: A round open space in a town
senses.definition: a round open area where several streets meet
senses.definitionCN: 几条街道交汇处的圆形开阔地
senses.example: Piccadilly Circus is a busy junction in London.
senses.exampleCN: 皮卡迪利广场是伦敦繁忙的路口。
senses.why: Roman circuses were long oval arenas.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马的竞技场是狭长的椭圆形。

senses.title: A noisy public spectacle
senses.definition: an event that becomes confusing and widely watched
senses.definitionCN: 变得混乱又广受围观的事件
senses.example: The trial turned into a media circus.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审判变成了媒体炒作。
senses.why: The noise of the show became a metaphor for confusion.
senses.whyCN: 表演的喧闹成了混乱的比喻。

intro.en: Circus begins as a Roman racecourse and ends as a word for public noise.
intro.cn: circus 从罗马赛马场开始，最后指公众的喧闹。

items.en: Circus means a ring or circle.
items.cn: circus 意为圆环、圆圈。

items.en: Roman circuses staged chariot races in long ovals.
items.cn: 古罗马竞技场在狭长椭圆场地办战车赛。

items.en: Travelling shows adopt the name for their round ring.
items.cn: 十八世纪巡回演出用它称呼圆形场地。

items.en: Big tops, clowns and acrobats define the modern show.
items.cn: 大帐篷、小丑与杂技构成现代马戏。

items.en: A noisy public event is called a circus.
items.cn: 喧闹的公共事件被称为 circus。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the circ- shape; the near-meaning group names other public shows.
note.cn: 形近组共享 circ- 词形；近义组列出其他公共演出。

entries.definition: A path that goes round.
A perfectly round line.
Shaped like a circle.
A public party with music and costumes.
A travelling event with rides and stalls.
An impressive public display.

normalIntro.en: A circus is a circle of noise under a round tent.
normalIntro.cn: 马戏就是圆帐篷下的一圈喧闹。

normal.en: Circus and circle share a root.
normal.cn: circus 与 circle 同源。

normal.en: The ring is round.
normal.cn: 场地是圆的。

normal.en: Clowns run round the ring.
normal.cn: 小丑绕着圆场跑。

normal.en: A crowd gathers in a circle.
normal.cn: 人群围成一圈。

normal.en: Too much noise becomes a media circus.
normal.cn: 噪音过多就成了媒体炒作。

abstract.en: A circle that laughs.
abstract.cn: 一个会笑的圆。

abstract.en: Lights running round a ring.
abstract.cn: 绕着圆环奔跑的灯光。

abstract.en: A town square turned into a stage.
abstract.cn: 城镇广场变成舞台。

examples.en: The circus travels from town to town in summer.
examples.cn: 夏天马戏团在各城镇间巡回演出。

examples.en: Oxford Circus is a busy shopping junction.
examples.cn: 牛津广场是繁忙的购物路口。

examples.en: The press turned the wedding into a circus.
examples.cn: 媒体把婚礼变成了闹哄哄的场面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟克斯」——圆场里人声鼎沸，马戏开演。

root: 拉丁 circus（圆环、竞技场）→ 英语 circus

sensesIntro.en: From a race ring to a tent ring to a ring of cameras.
sensesIntro.cn: 从赛马圆场到帐篷圆场，再到一圈镜头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round ring of sawdust under a tent
core.cn: 核心意象：帐篷下撒着木屑的圆形场地

branches.en: A clown waving from a ring.
branches.cn: 从圆场里挥手的小丑。

branches.en: Acrobats climbing under canvas.
branches.cn: 在帆布下攀爬的杂技演员。

branches.en: A round junction full of buses.
branches.cn: 挤满公交车的圆形路口。

branches.en: Cameras crowding a courtroom door.
branches.cn: 挤在法庭门口的摄像机。

branches.en: A show that the whole city watches.
branches.cn: 全城围观的表演。

intro.en: Circus is a Latin loan; the list adds words of rings and of shows.
intro.cn: circus 是拉丁借词；下面列出圆环与演出词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin circus is a ring, arena is sand, and spectaculum is a show.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circus 意为圆环，arena 意为沙地，spectaculum 意为演出。

latinEntries.exampleCN: circus 产生 circus 与 circular。
arena 产生 arena 与 arenas。
spectaculum 产生 spectacle 与 spectacular。

definition_zh: 引用；举出；传唤
definition_en: to quote a source, to give something as an example or proof, or to order someone to appear in court
core_image: 论文脚注里列出的一个个人名与书名
scene: 论文写到最后，作者逐条核对来源。She cited three studies in the first paragraph.
sceneCN: 这里 cited 是 cite 的过去式，指「引用」（第 1 个义项：提到他人的话或文字作为依据）；句意是她在第一段引用了三项研究。

senses.title: To quote a source
senses.definition: to mention words or writing from another source as support
senses.definitionCN: 提到他人的话语或文字作为依据
senses.example: She cited three studies in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一段引用了三项研究。
senses.why: Latin citare meant to call, and calling a writer into your text became quoting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 citare 意为召唤，把作者召进自己的文章便成了引用。

senses.title: To give as proof
senses.definition: to mention something as an example or as proof
senses.definitionCN: 举出某事物作为例子或证据
senses.example: He cited the falling sales as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 他举出销量下滑作为警告。
senses.why: A summoned witness and a summoned fact both serve as proof.
senses.whyCN: 被召来的证人与被召来的事实，都是用来作证的。

senses.title: To summon to court
senses.definition: to order someone to appear in a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人出庭
senses.example: The driver was cited for speeding.
senses.exampleCN: 那名司机因超速被传唤。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal: to call a person before a judge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思属法律：把人叫到法官面前。

intro.en: Cite began as a Latin verb for summoning a person.
intro.cn: cite 最初是一个表示传唤人的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Ciere meant to set something in motion.
items.cn: ciere 意为使某物动起来。

items.en: Citare meant to call or to summon someone.
items.cn: citare 意为呼唤或传唤某人。

items.en: Citer narrowed to calling a person to court.
items.cn: citer 的词义收窄为传人出庭。

items.en: English cite kept the legal summons and added quoting.
items.cn: 英语 cite 保留法律传唤，又添上引用的意思。

items.en: Scholarship made citing sources an everyday act.
items.cn: 学术写作让引用出处成了日常动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of cite, while the meaning group names quoting and summoning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cite 的读音，近义组列出引用与传唤。

entries.definition: a place where something is built
the ability to see
a tool with a long blade for cutting grass
to repeat the words of a source
to mention a source in a text
to order someone to appear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the three same-sound words, the court origin and the academic habit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用三个同音词、法庭来源以及学术习惯。

normal.en: Cite, site and sight sound alike, so check which one you wrote.
normal.cn: cite、site 与 sight 读音相同，写完要检查用的是哪一个。

normal.en: The oldest cite is a court summons, which is why a speeding driver is cited.
normal.cn: 最古老的 cite 是法庭传唤，所以超速司机会被 cite。

normal.en: To cite a study is to call the researchers into your own paragraph.
normal.cn: cite a study 就是把研究者召进你自己的段落。

normal.en: Citation is the noun, covering a footnote, a prize and a summons.
normal.cn: citation 是名词，涵盖脚注、表彰与传唤。

normal.en: Citing reasons is citing proof, not quoting words.
normal.cn: cite reasons 是举出证据，不是引用原话。

abstract.en: Picture a name in small print at the bottom of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象页面底部一行小字里的一个人名。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raising a folder to show one page in court.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上一只手举起文件夹，翻出其中一页。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon pinned on a coat for bravery.
abstract.cn: 想象外套上为表彰勇敢而别上的绶带。

examples.en: Please cite the original article, not the summary.
examples.cn: 请引用原始文章，而不是摘要。

examples.en: The report cites rising costs as the main cause.
examples.cn: 报告举出成本上升作为主要原因。

examples.en: Two officers were cited for their courage.
examples.cn: 两名警官因勇敢受到表彰。

dict_mnemonic.text: cite 与 site、sight 同音：写论文时要看清是引用、地点还是看见。

root: 源自拉丁语 citare（召唤），是 ciere（使动）的反复形式，本指传唤出庭，后转指引用。

sensesIntro.en: A court summons gives the idea of calling something in, which supplies both the quoted source and the proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 法庭传唤先给出「召来」的意思，由此生出被引的原文与被举的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name listed in small print under a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：页面下方用小字列出的一个名字。

branches.en: Quoting is the everyday sense in study and writing.
branches.cn: 引用是学习与写作中最日常的义项。

branches.en: Citing proof calls a fact into the argument.
branches.cn: 举出证据就是把一项事实召进论证。

branches.en: The court summons is the oldest sense still in use.
branches.cn: 法庭传唤是仍在使用的最古老义项。

branches.en: A quoted source and a cited fact both support a claim.
branches.cn: 被引的原文与被举的事实都支撑一个主张。

branches.en: Citation can mean praise as well as a summons.
branches.cn: citation 既可指传唤，也可指表彰。

intro.en: The short stem builds a noun, two adjectives and the whole citation family.
intro.cn: 这个短词干构成名词、两个形容词以及整个 citation 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin citare and its base ciere supply the -ate pattern behind cite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 citare 及其词基 ciere 提供了 cite 背后的 -ate 构词模式。

items.example: Cite the page number as well.
The judge cited the earlier ruling.
items.exampleCN: 法官援引了先前的裁决。

items.example: He was citing a long report.
items.exampleCN: 他正在引用一份长报告。
这篇论文有五十条引文。

latinEntries.example: Citare is the direct source of cite.
latinEntries.exampleCN: citare 是 cite 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Ciere is the older base of citare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ciere 是 citare 更古老的词基。

definition_zh: 公民的；民事的；文明的；国内的
definition_en: relating to the private rights of citizens, polite and well mannered, or happening inside one country
core_image: 法庭上两边各坐一人，中间没有刀剑
scene: 两位邻居为一道篱笆争了很久，最后走进法庭。The two families settled the dispute through civil action.
sceneCN: 这里 civil 指「民事的」（第 1 个义项：与公民私人权利有关的）；句意是两家通过民事诉讼解决了争端。

pos.zh: 公民的；民事的；文明的；国内的

senses.title: Relating to private citizens
senses.definition: relating to the private rights of citizens rather than to crime or the army
senses.definitionCN: 与公民私人权利有关，而非刑事或军事
senses.example: The case went to a civil court.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案子提交民事法庭审理。
senses.why: Latin civilis meant of a citizen, and citizen law grew beside military and criminal law.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 civilis 意为公民的，公民之法与军事、刑法并列而生。

senses.title: Polite and well mannered
senses.definition: polite and respectful in behaviour towards others
senses.definitionCN: 举止有礼并尊重他人
senses.example: He gave a civil answer even under attack.
senses.exampleCN: 即使受到攻击，他的回答依然有礼。
senses.why: Life in a citizen community required courtesy between equals.
senses.whyCN: 公民共同体中的生活要求平等者之间以礼相待。

senses.title: Inside one country
senses.definition: happening between groups within the same country

senses.example: The country suffered a long civil war.

senses.title: An advanced human society
senses.definition: a society with cities, writing, industry and organised government
senses.definitionCN: 拥有城市、文字、手工业与有组织政府的社会
senses.example: Ancient civilizations grew up along great rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 古代文明在大河沿岸发展起来。
senses.why: Farm surpluses freed people to build cities and keep written records, and that whole package became the mark of a civilization.
senses.whyCN: 农业剩余让人腾出手来建城市、留文字记录，这一整套就成了文明的标志。

senses.title: The stage of social development
senses.definition: the stage of social development that such societies have reached
senses.definitionCN: 这类社会所达到的社会发展阶段
senses.example: Trade and writing pushed the region towards civilization.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易与文字把这一地区推向了文明。

senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也指达到的阶段，是抽象层次而不是某个具体社会。

senses.title: The culture of a place or period

definition_zh: adj. 穿着…衣服的；被…覆盖的（常用于复合词）
definition_en: dressed in a particular way, or covered with something
core_image: 矿工们裹着厚厚的工装走下矿井
scene: 矿工们穿着厚重的防护服，走进幽深的矿井。The miners, clad in heavy suits, entered the dark shaft.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clad 指穿着…衣服的；句意是矿工们穿着厚重的防护服，走进幽深的矿井。

senses.title: Dressed in a particular way
senses.definition: wearing clothes of a stated kind
senses.definitionCN: 穿着某种特定衣物
senses.example: She was clad in black silk from head to foot.
senses.exampleCN: 她从头上到脚下都穿着黑绸。
senses.why: Clad is the old past participle of clothe, used as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: clad 是 clothe 的古老过去分词，用作形容词。

senses.title: Covered with something
senses.definition: covered or coated with a substance
senses.definitionCN: 被某种物质覆盖或包住
senses.example: The hills were clad in fresh snow.
senses.exampleCN: 山丘覆盖着新雪。
senses.why: The sense moved from clothes to any covering.
senses.whyCN: 词义从衣服扩展到任何覆盖物。

intro.en: Clad is an old past form of clothe that became an adjective of covering.
intro.cn: clad 是 clothe 的古老过去式，后来成为表示覆盖的形容词。

items.en: Clathian means to clothe.
items.cn: 古英语 clathian 意为给…穿衣。

items.en: Clad serves as past tense and past participle.
items.cn: 中古英语 clad 作过去式与过去分词。

items.en: Writers use clad before nouns, as in clad in wool.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家把 clad 用在名词前，如 clad in wool。

items.en: Snow-clad and armour-clad become common.
items.cn: 十九世纪 snow-clad、armour-clad 流行。

items.en: Clad survives mainly in formal and poetic prose.
items.cn: 现代 clad 多见于正式与文学语体。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names other ways of being dressed.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组列出穿衣的其他说法。

entries.definition: A lump of earth.
Happy about something.
A device that grips.
Wearing clothes of a kind.
Wearing clothes; covered.
Dressed, often formally.

normalIntro.en: Clad is what clothe leaves behind: the dressed person.
normalIntro.cn: clad 就是 clothe 留下的结果：穿好衣的人。

normal.en: Clothe turns into clad.
normal.cn: clothe 变成 clad。

normal.en: Clad in white means dressed in white.
normal.cn: clad in white 意为穿白衣。

normal.en: Add a noun to make compounds.
normal.cn: 加名词构成复合词。

normal.en: Snow-clad hills are covered in snow.
normal.cn: snow-clad 的山是被雪覆盖的山。

normal.en: Clad is literary, not everyday casual.
normal.cn: clad 偏文学，不用于日常口语。

abstract.en: Cloth frozen into a description.
abstract.cn: 布料凝固成一个形容词。

abstract.en: A hill wearing a white coat.
abstract.cn: 披着白外套的山。

abstract.en: Dressing that became covering.
abstract.cn: 从穿衣变成覆盖。

examples.en: The dancers were clad in silver and white.
examples.cn: 舞者们穿着银白相间的衣服。

examples.en: He arrived clad only in shorts and sandals.
examples.cn: 他来时只穿短裤和凉鞋。

examples.en: The valley lay clad in morning mist.
examples.cn: 山谷笼罩在晨雾之中。

dict_mnemonic.text: clothe 的过去分词 clad → 被衣服「包住」的状态，即穿着与覆盖。

root: 古英语 clathian（给…穿衣）→ 中古英语 clad（过去式/过去分词）→ 形容词 clad

sensesIntro.en: The same past form describes people in clothes and hills in snow.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个过去式既写穿衣的人，也写覆雪的山。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy coat wrapped round a miner
core.cn: 核心意象：厚外套裹住一名矿工

branches.en: A dancer in silver silk.
branches.cn: 穿银绸的舞者。

branches.en: A traveller in shorts and sandals.
branches.cn: 穿短裤凉鞋的旅人。

branches.en: A hill under fresh snow.
branches.cn: 新雪覆盖的山丘。

branches.cn: 晨雾笼罩的山谷。

branches.en: A body wearing something as a layer.
branches.cn: 以某一层包裹身体。

intro.en: Clad belongs to a small family of dressing words; the list adds covering and wearing terms.
intro.cn: clad 属于一小族穿衣词；下面列出覆盖与穿着的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis is a garment and tegere is to cover.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis 意为衣服，tegere 意为覆盖。

latinEntries.exampleCN: vestis 产生 vest 与 invest。
tegere 产生 integument 与 tegument。
clathian 产生 clothe 与 clad。

definition_zh: 声称；断言；索取；认领；主张；权利要求
definition_en: to say that something is true when others may doubt it, to ask for something as your right, or a right that you say you have
core_image: 一只手举着一张写有自己名字的单据
scene: 保险员把表格推过来，笔尖停在签名处。Two men claim the same wallet at the front desk.
sceneCN: 这里 claim 指「认领」（第 2 个义项：主张某物归自己所有）；句意是两个男人在前台都声称那个钱包是自己的。

senses.title: To state as true
senses.definition: to say that something is true when other people may not believe it
senses.definitionCN: 在别人可能不相信时仍说某事为真
senses.example: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。
senses.why: The old verb meant to cry out, so a claim is something said loudly and publicly.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老动词本指大声喊出，因此 claim 是被大声公开说出来的话。

senses.title: To demand as your own
senses.definition: to ask for something that you believe belongs to you by right
senses.definitionCN: 要求得到你认为按权利属于自己的东西
senses.example: He claimed his luggage at the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在柜台认领了自己的行李。
senses.why: A public cry for something became a formal demand for property or payment.
senses.whyCN: 公开喊出某物，演变成对财产或款项的正式要求。

senses.title: A right or a demand
senses.definition: a statement that you have a right to something, or that right itself
senses.definitionCN: 关于你有权得到某物的声明，或该项权利本身
senses.example: Her claim to the land was never proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这块土地的所有权主张从未得到证实。
senses.why: The noun took the same shape as the verb and named the demand rather than the act of demanding.
senses.whyCN: 名词与动词同形，但它指所提的要求，而不是提出要求的动作。

intro.en: Claim comes from a Latin verb meaning to cry out, which also gave English exclaim and proclaim.
intro.cn: claim 出自拉丁语中表示大声喊出的动词，exclaim 与 proclaim 也来自它。

items.en: Clamare meant to cry out or call loudly.
items.cn: clamare 意为大声喊叫或呼喊。

items.en: Clamer carried the sense of calling out a demand.
items.cn: clamer 带有喊出一项要求的含义。

items.en: English took the word as claimen in law and argument.
items.cn: 英语以 claimen 的形式把它用于法律与辩论。

items.en: A claim became a formal demand for land or money.
items.cn: claim 成为对土地或金钱的正式要求。

items.en: The verb widened to plain statements of fact.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到对事实的普通陈述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words with a similar shape, while the meaning group holds verbs of saying and demanding.
note.cn: 形近组列出外形相近的短词，近义组列出言说与要求类动词。

entries.definition: a tool that holds things tightly together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西紧紧夹住的工具

entries.definition: to hold something firmly with your hand
to praise someone loudly and publicly
to state something firmly as a fact
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地把某事说成事实

entries.definition: to announce something officially or clearly
entries.definitionCN: 正式或清楚地宣布某事

entries.definition: to ask for something very firmly

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cry-out root, the legal demand and the noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用呼喊词根、法律要求以及名动同形这三条线。

normal.en: Claim belongs with exclaim and proclaim; all three contain the Latin cry for a call.
normal.cn: claim 与 exclaim、proclaim 同族，三者都含拉丁语表示喊叫的部分。

normal.en: To claim is to put your hand up in public, either to speak or to take.
normal.cn: claim 就是在公开场合举手，要么发言，要么拿东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same, so a claim is both the act and the thing demanded.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，所以 claim 既是动作，也是所要求的对象。

normal.en: Insurance papers are full of claims, because a claim asks for money.
normal.cn: 保险文件里满是 claim，因为这个词可以指索赔。

normal.en: Lay claim to is the fixed phrase for ownership, not for an opinion.
normal.cn: lay claim to 是表示所有权的固定说法，不用来说看法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised at an auction with a numbered card.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖会上举起一只拿着号牌的手。

abstract.en: Picture a luggage tag matching the name on a passport.
abstract.cn: 想象一张行李牌与护照上的名字对得上。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary line drawn on a map and then disputed.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画出一条边界线，随后被人争执。

examples.en: She claims the keys were left on the desk.
examples.cn: 她声称钥匙是落在桌子上的。

examples.en: He claimed his luggage at the counter before the taxi came.
examples.cn: 出租车来之前，他在柜台认领了行李。

examples.en: The company made a claim for the damaged goods.
examples.cn: 公司就受损货物提出了索赔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cl 想成「喊」，aim 想成「目标」：朝着目标喊一声，就是声明这东西归我。

root: 源自拉丁语 clamare（大声喊叫），经古法语 clamer 进入英语，本义是喊出自己的权利。

sensesIntro.en: A loud cry turns into an assertion, then into a demand, and finally into the right behind the demand.
sensesIntro.cn: 一声大喊先变成断言，再变成索求，最后变成索求背后的权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand holding a paper with a name on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手拿着写有名字的纸。

branches.en: The old cry becomes a public statement of fact.
branches.cn: 古老的呼喊变成公开的事实陈述。

branches.en: The same cry becomes a request for what is yours.
branches.cn: 同样的呼喊变成对属于自己之物的索求。

branches.en: The noun names the demand and the right behind it.
branches.cn: 名词指所提的要求以及其背后的权利。

branches.en: Saying and taking share one verb because both are public acts.
branches.cn: 言说与索取共用一个动词，因为两者都是公开行为。

branches.en: A claim needs a right, and a right survives only if claimed.
branches.cn: 索求需要权利，而权利只有被主张才存在。

intro.en: One short verb grows a plural, two participles, an agent noun and two prefixed forms.
intro.cn: 一个短动词长出复数、两个分词、一个施动名词和两个前缀形式。

latinIntro.en: The base clamare also underlies exclaim, proclaim and acclaim, all built with Latin prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 clamare 也是 exclaim、proclaim、acclaim 的来源，这些词都加了拉丁语前缀。

items.meaning: to state true or demand as a right
items.example: He will claim the seat by the window.

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.example: She claims to know the answer.
They claimed the land in court.
items.exampleCN: 他们在法庭上主张这块土地。

items.example: He is claiming the reward today.

items.meaning: a person who makes a claim

items.example: They reclaimed the field from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们围海造出了那片田。

items.example: The site carries a short disclaimer.
items.exampleCN: 这个网站附有一份简短免责声明。

latinEntries.example: Clamare gave English claim and exclaim.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clamare 给了英语 claim 与 exclaim。

definition_zh: n. 蛤蜊，蛤肉；v. （口语）闭嘴，守口如瓶
definition_en: a shellfish that lives in sand; informal, to refuse to speak
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上，一只蛤蜊冒出小水柱
scene: 退潮后，孩子们在湿沙里挖蛤蜊。At low tide the children dug for clams in the wet sand.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clam 指蛤蜊；句意是退潮后孩子们在湿沙里挖蛤蜊。

senses.title: A burrowing shellfish
senses.definition: a soft-bodied shellfish with a hinged shell that lives in sand
senses.definitionCN: 带铰合壳、生活在沙中的软体贝类
senses.example: We gathered clams at the water edge.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在水边捡蛤蜊。
senses.why: The shell closes tightly, which suggested the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 蛤壳紧闭，启发了第二个义项。

senses.title: To refuse to speak
senses.definition: informal, to stay silent and give nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 口语，保持沉默，什么也不透露
senses.example: He clammed up when the police arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 警察一到，他就闭口不言了。
senses.why: The shut shell became a picture of a closed mouth.
senses.whyCN: 紧闭的壳成了闭嘴的形象。

intro.en: Clam first meant a grip or bond, then the shellfish that grips its shell shut.
intro.cn: clam 最初指抓握、束缚，后指紧紧合壳的贝类。

items.en: Clam means a bond or grip.
items.cn: 古英语 clam 意为束缚、抓握。

items.en: The word names a shell that clamps shut.
items.cn: 十六世纪用它指紧紧合壳的贝类。

items.en: Clam chowder spreads with American cooking.
items.cn: 十九世纪蛤蜊浓汤随美国烹饪传播。

items.en: The idiom clammed up means to fall silent.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现 clammed up 的沉默义。

items.en: The food sense and the idiom both survive.
items.cn: 现代的食用义与习语义都保留着。

note.en: The look-alike group is one letter from clam; the near-meaning group names other shellfish.

normal.en: Clam and clamp feel alike.

normal.en: Sand hides the clam.

normal.en: Its shell shuts tight.
normal.cn: 它的壳紧紧合上。

normal.en: A silent suspect clams up.
normal.cn: 沉默的嫌疑人闭口不言。

normal.en: Chowder is made from clams.

abstract.cn: 一张贝壳做的嘴。

abstract.en: Secrets kept in wet sand.

abstract.en: A hinge that refuses to open.

examples.en: The tide left a row of small clams on the beach.
examples.cn: 潮水在沙滩上留下一排小蛤蜊。

examples.en: She made clam chowder for Sunday lunch.
examples.cn: 她做了蛤蜊浓汤当周日午餐。

examples.en: He clammed up as soon as the topic came up.
examples.cn: 一谈到这个话题，他就闭口不言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 蛤蜊合壳 → 人闭嘴；clam up 即「像蛤蜊一样封口」。

root: 古英语 clam（束缚、抓握）→ 十六世纪指合壳贝类 clam

sensesIntro.en: From a tight grip to a tight shell to a tight mouth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从抓紧，到紧壳，再到紧闭的嘴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small shell breathing in wet sand
core.cn: 核心意象：湿沙里缓缓吐水的贝壳

branches.en: A clam spouting water at low tide.
branches.cn: 退潮时吐水的蛤蜊。

branches.en: A bowl of chowder on a table.
branches.cn: 桌上的一碗浓汤。

branches.en: A suspect staring at the floor.
branches.cn: 盯着地板的嫌疑人。

branches.en: A witness refusing questions.
branches.cn: 拒绝回答的证人。

branches.en: A shell and a mouth both closed.
branches.cn: 同样紧闭的壳与嘴。

intro.en: Clam is a short English word; the list adds shellfish and sea words.

definition_zh: n. 夹钳，夹具；（英）车轮锁；v. 夹紧；强制实施，严厉打击
definition_en: a tool that holds things tightly; to hold firmly or enforce strictly
core_image: 木匠用铁夹把两块木板死死扣在一起
scene: 木匠用一只铁夹把两块木板固定好。The carpenter used a clamp to hold the two boards together.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clamp 指夹具；句意是木匠用一只铁夹把两块木板固定好。

senses.title: A device that grips things
senses.definition: a tool that holds two or more things tightly together
senses.definitionCN: 把两件或多件东西紧紧夹住的工具
senses.example: Tighten the clamp around the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 把管道上的夹具拧紧。
senses.why: The word comes from a clasp or grip.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自「扣紧、抓握」之义。

senses.title: To fasten tightly
senses.definition: to press or hold something firmly in place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢压住或固定
senses.example: He clamped the wood to the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木料夹在工作台上。
senses.why: A clamp as a noun became a verb of gripping.
senses.whyCN: 名词夹具演变为抓握动词。

senses.title: To enforce strictly
senses.definition: to put a firm stop or limit on an activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某种活动施加严格的限制或制止
senses.example: The city clamped down on illegal parking.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市严打违章停车。
senses.why: The grip image became a metaphor for control.
senses.whyCN: 夹紧的形象成了管制的比喻。

intro.en: Clamp begins as a clasp of metal and grows into a verb of control.
intro.cn: clamp 从金属扣件出发，发展为管制的动词。

items.en: Clamp names a clasp or brace.
items.cn: 十六世纪 clamp 指扣件、支撑件。

items.en: The word is related to Dutch klampe, a clasp.
items.cn: 它与荷兰语 klampe（扣件）相关。

items.en: Woodworkers use clamps to hold boards.
items.cn: 十七世纪木匠用夹具固定木板。

definition_zh: 氏族；大家族；帮派团伙；游戏中的公会
definition_en: a group of people who claim descent from a common ancestor and act as one social unit, or a close group with a shared interest
core_image: 一群人围在一起清点祖先的名字，把家谱铺在桌上。
scene: 山脚下的老屋里，族人围坐，把家谱铺在桌上，逐代念出祖先的名字并核对辈分。The elders of the clan keep the genealogy in a wooden chest and read it aloud at every wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 clan 指「共享祖先、以血缘联结的氏族」（第 1 个义项：以共同祖先为纽带的群体）；句意为族中长者把族谱收在木箱里，每逢婚礼就当众诵读。可辨识物件：家谱、木箱、老屋、围坐的族人。

derivatives.zh: clan + -ish（形容词后缀）→ 抱团排外的，语义落在群体内部的紧密与排他
clannish + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以抱团排外的方式，语义仅改词性
clannish + -ness（名词后缀）→ 抱团排外的性质，语义抽象化为品质
clan + 连接成分 -s + man（人）→ 同氏族成员，语义落在成员身份
clan + -ship（状态后缀）→ 氏族归属与氏族制度，语义由群体转为制度

senses.title: A group tracing one ancestor
senses.definition: a social unit whose members claim descent from a common ancestor and recognize shared obligations
senses.definitionCN: 成员自称出自同一祖先、并承认相互义务的社会单位
senses.example: The whole clan gathers at the ancestral hall each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，整个氏族都在祠堂聚会。
senses.why: Scots clann originally meant 'children, family', so the first sense is a family widened to all who claim one ancestor.
senses.whyCN: 苏格兰语 clann 原意是「子女、家族」，因此第一义就是把家庭扩展到所有自称同祖的人。

senses.title: An extended family network
senses.definition: the practical network of relatives who help one another with money, labour and marriages
senses.definitionCN: 在经济、劳力与婚姻上互相帮衬的亲属关系网络
senses.example: The marriage joined two clans that had traded for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这场婚姻把两个通商百年的家族连在一起。
senses.why: a clan in daily use is less a pedigree than a set of people you can call on, so the kin group becomes a support network.
senses.whyCN: 日常所说的 clan 与其说是一份谱系，不如说是一群可以求助的人，于是血亲团体变成了互助网络。

senses.title: A tribal division under a chief
senses.titleCN: 部落之下由首领统辖的分支
senses.definition: a subdivision of a tribe, usually led by a chief or a council of elders
senses.definitionCN: 部落之下的分支，通常由首领或长老会领导
senses.example: Each clan sent one elder to the tribal council.
senses.exampleCN: 每个氏族派一名长老参加部落议事会。
senses.why: anthropology needed a unit between the single household and the whole tribe, and the old family word took that place.
senses.whyCN: 人类学需要在单户家庭与整个部落之间找一个单位，旧的「家族」词就占了这个位置。

senses.title: A close exclusive faction
senses.definition: a small group of colleagues or friends who promote one another and keep outsiders at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 互相提携、对圈外人保持距离的同事或朋友小圈子
senses.example: The department is run by a clan of people who lunch together.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门由一个总在一起吃午饭的小圈子把持。
senses.why: the family image is borrowed with irony: the group behaves as if related, and its warmth excludes.
senses.whyCN: 借用了家庭的意象并带讽刺：这群人表现得像亲戚，其温情同时排斥外人。

senses.title: A criminal or street gang
senses.definition: an organized criminal group that protects its members and demands loyalty above the law
senses.definitionCN: 保护成员、要求忠诚高于法律的有组织犯罪团体
senses.example: Police linked the warehouse fire to a clan fighting over the docks.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把仓库大火与一个争夺码头的帮派联系起来。
senses.why: loyalty, silence and inherited membership look like kinship rules, so the word moves easily from family to gang.
senses.whyCN: 忠诚、缄默与世袭身份都像亲属规则，因此这个词很容易从家族滑向帮派。

senses.title: A gaming guild of players
senses.definition: an in-game association of players who share a name, a chat channel and joint activities
senses.definitionCN: 共享名称、聊天频道与集体活动的游戏内玩家组织
senses.example: Our clan meets online every Friday to raid together.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的公会每周五上线，一起团队副本。
senses.why: online groups revive the old feature of a shared name and mutual aid, so players borrowed the word whole.
senses.whyCN: 线上群体恢复了共享名称与互助的旧特点，因此玩家把整个词借了过去。

senses.title: A biological lineage
senses.definition: a set of individuals or cell lines descended from one common ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 由一个共同祖先传下来的个体集合或细胞系
senses.example: All the mice in the study belong to a single clan.
senses.exampleCN: 研究中的全部小鼠都属于同一个世系。
senses.why: genetics kept only the descent component of the word and dropped the social obligations.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学只保留了这个词的「传承」成分，去掉了社会义务。

senses.title: An in-group sharing taste or habit
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：共享品味或习惯的内群体
senses.definition: any loose in-group defined by a shared taste, jargon or routine rather than by kinship
senses.definitionCN: 由共同品味、行话或习惯而非血亲界定出来的松散内群体
senses.example: The film has become a clan of people who quote it daily.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影已经成了一个每天引用台词的圈子。
senses.why: once the word means any close group, kinship can drop out entirely and only the boundary remains.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词泛指任何紧密群体，血亲关系就可完全脱落，只剩边界。

intro.en: Clan came into English from Scottish Gaelic clann 'children, family', which goes back to Old Irish cland and, through borrowing, to Latin planta 'sprout, plant'.
intro.cn: clan 从苏格兰盖尔语 clann「子女、家族」进入英语，上承古爱尔兰语 cland，再往上经借用关系连到拉丁 planta「芽、植株」。

items.en: Planta meant 'sprout, shoot, plant'; the image is a shoot growing from one stock, which is also how a lineage is pictured.
items.cn: planta 意为「芽、新枝、植株」；意象是从同一根桩上长出的新枝，血统也正以此取象。

items.en: The Latin noun was taken into early Celtic as a word for offspring or family; the exact route is source uncertain, and no single borrowing path is agreed.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词被早期凯尔特语借去，用来指后代或家族；具体路径来源不确定，学界并无一致说法。

items.en: Old Irish cland is recorded with the sense 'family, offspring'; from it comes the Gaelic form that English later took.
items.cn: 古爱尔兰语 cland 有「家族、后代」的义项记录；盖尔语形式即由其而来，英语后来又借入这个盖尔语形式。

items.en: Scottish Gaelic clann kept the meaning 'children, family' and was used for a group claiming one ancestor, without any claim to a separate race.
items.cn: 苏格兰盖尔语 clann 保留「子女、家族」之义，用来指自称同祖的一群人，并不含「另一个种族」的意思。

items.en: English took the word in the late Middle Ages for Highland kin groups; the wider senses of faction and guild are much later extensions.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期借入此词，指高地亲族团体；小集团与公会等更宽的义项是很晚的延伸。

items.en: The sense 'race' sometimes read into the word is a later misunderstanding; dictionaries stress descent and loyalty, not biology.
items.cn: 有时被人读进这个词的「种族」义属后来误解；词典强调的是世系与忠诚，而非生物学。

note.en: Group one holds words whose form is close but whose root is different; group two holds real kin-group terms that differ in scale or in the tie invoked.
note.cn: 第一组是形近而词根不同的词；第二组是真正的亲族词，差别在规模或所诉诸的纽带。

entries.definition: A shellfish or the shell itself; its own origin is source uncertain, and it has no established link to clan beyond a similar shape and short vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 蛤蜊或蛤壳，其自身来源不确定，除拼写与短元音外与 clan 并无确立的联系。

entries.definition: A device that holds things tightly; its origin is not established as the same as clan's, and only the opening sounds coincide.
entries.definitionCN: 夹紧器；其来源是否与 clan 相同并无定论，只共享开头音，不能据此认为同源。

entries.definition: A homophone often confused with clan; the organisation it names is entirely different, and any historical link between the two words is source uncertain.
entries.definitionCN: 与 clan 同音、常被混淆的词；它所称的组织完全不同，两词之间是否有历史联系则来源不确定。

entries.definition: From Greek klōn 'twig, slip', a cutting used to propagate a plant; the 'twig' picture is the only faint echo of clan.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语 klōn「枝条、插穗」，指用来繁殖植物的切枝；只有「枝条」意象与 clan 隐约相像。

entries.definition: A larger group of clans or bands united by a common name and leadership; a clan is one unit inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 由多个氏族或部落分支联合而成、共享名称与领导的更大群体；clan 是其中一个单位。

entries.definition: A line of descent traced from an ancestor; it stresses genealogy and may have no corporate action or territory.
entries.definitionCN: 从某位祖先追下来的世系；强调谱系，未必有集体行动或领地。

entries.definition: One's relatives taken together, without a clan name, a chief or a common ritual.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人全部亲属的集合，没有氏族名称、首领或共同仪式。

entries.definition: Relatives beyond the nuclear household who cooperate in daily life; the term is domestic, while a clan may hold land and feuds.
entries.definitionCN: 核心家庭之外、在日常生活中互助的亲属；这个词属家庭层面，而氏族可拥有土地与世仇。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Gaelic source, the Latin plant image, and the words English built on clan.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的盖尔语来源、拉丁「植株」意象，以及英语在 clan 之上造出的词。

normal.en: Gaelic clann 'children': a clan is a family written large.
normal.cn: 盖尔语 clann「子女」：氏族就是一个放大了的家庭。

normal.en: Latin planta 'sprout' sits at the far end of the borrowing chain: one stock, many shoots.
normal.cn: 借用链的最远端是拉丁 planta「芽」：一根桩，许多新枝。

normal.en: clan + -ish gives clannish, the everyday adjective for a group that keeps others out.
normal.cn: clan 加 -ish 得到 clannish，是形容群体排外的日常形容词。

normal.en: Clansman and clanship mark the member and the system.
normal.cn: clansman 与 clanship 分别标记成员与制度。

normal.en: The fixed phrase 'the head of the clan' shows how a group is imagined as one body.
normal.cn: 固定搭配「族长」显示这群人被想象成一个身体。

abstract.en: Picture a name that everyone in the room shares and no outsider may use.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字，屋里人人共有，外人不得使用。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that passes to children who never agreed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债，传给从未同意过的孩子。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree with roots below the soil, where nobody can see where it began.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树，根埋在土下，无人看得见它从何处起头。

examples.en: The clan still owns the terraced fields below the village.
examples.cn: 这个氏族至今拥有村下的梯田。

examples.en: In the game, a clan can hold a fortress only if its members log in together.
examples.cn: 在游戏里，公会只有成员一起上线才能占据堡垒。

examples.en: The novelist describes a political clan that treats the ministry as family property.
examples.cn: 小说家描写一个把部委当作家族财产的政治小集团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克蓝」：一族人都穿同一种蓝布衣，远远一看便知是自己人 → 氏族、家族、抱团的小集团

root: 苏格兰盖尔语 clann「子女、家族」< 古爱尔兰语 cland < 拉丁 planta「芽、植株」（借词链）；现代英语 clan。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread outward from one ancestor: a named descent group, then its living network, its place in a tribe, then groups that only imitate kinship, a gang, a gaming guild, a biological line and finally any in-group with a boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一位祖先向外扩散：有名号的世系群体，接着是它活生生的关系网、它在部落中的位置，然后是只模仿亲属关系的群体、帮派、游戏公会、生物世系，最后是任何有边界的内部圈子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ancestor's name, and everyone who answers to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个祖先的名字，以及所有应这个名字的人。

chain: PLACE THE GROUP IN A TRIBE

branches.en: DESCENT AND POLITICS: a named kin group and its standing inside a larger tribe.
branches.cn: 世系与政治：有名号的亲族群体，以及它在更大部落中的地位。

branches.en: LIVING NETWORK: the relatives one actually calls on for labour, money and marriage.
branches.cn: 活的关系网：真正能为劳力、金钱与婚姻去求助的那些亲戚。

branches.en: FAMILY IMITATED: factions and gangs borrow the loyalty and silence of kinship.
branches.cn: 被模仿的家庭：小集团与帮派借用了亲属关系的忠诚与缄默。

branches.en: VOLUNTARY BOUNDARY: guilds and taste groups keep the name and the inside/outside line.
branches.cn: 自愿的边界：公会与品味圈子保留了名称与内外界线。

branches.en: PURE LINEAGE: biology keeps only descent and lets the social duties fall away.
branches.cn: 纯世系：生物学只留下传承，让社会义务脱落。

intro.en: Clan itself is a borrowing, so its family is mostly English suffixes added to a Gaelic noun, with a Latin noun at the end of the borrowing chain.
intro.cn: clan 本身是借词，因此它的词族主要是加在这个盖尔语名词上的英语后缀，借用链末端则是一个拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is planta 'sprout, plant' with its verb plantare; Latin supplies no further relative of English clan except through this borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语一端是 planta「芽、植株」及其动词 plantare；除这条借用链之外，拉丁语并不提供英语 clan 的其他同族词。

items.example: The word entered English with no change of shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词以原来的形式整体进入英语。

items.meaning: loyal to one's group and cold to outsiders
items.example: The office felt clannish to a new arrival.
items.exampleCN: 新来的人觉得这间办公室很抱团排外。

items.example: The hiring was done clannishly, among cousins.
items.exampleCN: 招聘是在表亲之间抱团完成的。

items.example: Their clannishness kept good applicants away.
items.exampleCN: 他们的抱团排外把优秀申请者挡在门外。

items.example: A clansman carried the chief's banner.
items.exampleCN: 一名氏族成员扛着首领的旗帜。

items.example: Clanship shaped who could vote in the village.
items.exampleCN: 氏族归属决定了村里谁有投票权。

items.example: The Latin noun opens the borrowing chain.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是借用链的起点。

items.structure: plantare, plantavi, plantatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb describes putting a shoot into the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把新枝插进土里。

definition_zh: 澄清；阐明；使（液体）变清
definition_en: to make something easier to understand, or to make a liquid clear by removing the solids in it
core_image: 浑水静置后慢慢变透明
scene: 会议开到一半，投影上的数字互相矛盾。She asked him to clarify the second point before the vote.
sceneCN: 这里 clarify 指「澄清；阐明」（第 1 个义项：把不清楚的事说明白）；句意是她让他在表决前把第二点讲清楚。

senses.title: To make something understandable
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes clear and easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 加以解释，使某事变得清楚易懂
senses.example: The teacher clarified the rule with one example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一个例子把这个规则讲清楚了。
senses.why: The Latin base means bright, so to clarify is literally to make a matter bright.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基本义是明亮的，所以 clarify 字面上就是让事情变亮。

senses.title: To clear a liquid
senses.definition: to make a liquid clear by heating it or removing the solid bits
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热或去除固体微粒使液体变清
senses.example: Melt the butter and clarify it slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 把黄油化开，慢慢澄清。
senses.why: The same brightness image applies to a cloudy liquid that turns transparent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的明亮意象也用于由浑浊变透明的液体。

intro.en: Clarify is built on the Latin adjective for bright, the same root as clarity and clear.
intro.cn: clarify 建立在拉丁语表示明亮的形容词上，与 clarity、clear 同根。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, clear or famous.
items.cn: clarus 意为明亮的、清澈的或闻名的。

items.en: Clarificare meant to make bright or to make plain.
items.cn: clarificare 意为使明亮或使明白。

items.en: Clarifier carried the sense of explaining and of clearing liquid.
items.cn: clarifier 兼有解释与澄清液体的含义。

items.en: English took the verb as clarify in learned and kitchen use.
items.cn: 英语以 clarify 借入，用于学术与厨房两种场合。

items.en: The explaining sense now dominates in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 在日常语言中，解释义如今占主导。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the clarity family, while the meaning group names ways of making things plain.
note.cn: 形近组列出 clarity 家族，近义组列出使事情明白的各种说法。

entries.definition: the quality of being clear and easy to follow
easy to see through or to understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看透或容易理解的

entries.definition: an explanation that removes doubt
to tell someone how something works
entries.definitionCN: 告诉某人某事如何运作

entries.definition: to make something less complicated
to light something up or make it clear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bright root, the cloudy-liquid image and the -ify ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用明亮词根、浑浊液体的意象以及 -ify 后缀。

normal.en: Clarify shares its root with clear and clarity: all three carry brightness.
normal.cn: clarify 与 clear、clarity 同根，三者都带明亮的含义。

normal.en: To clarify is to switch on a lamp in a room where people are guessing.
normal.cn: clarify 就是在大家靠猜的房间里打开一盏灯。

normal.en: The -ify ending means to make, so clarify means to make clear.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ify 表示使成为，所以 clarify 就是使清楚。

normal.en: Butter can be clarified, and so can an argument.
normal.cn: 黄油可以澄清，争论也可以澄清。

normal.en: In meetings, clarify a point is more polite than you are wrong.
normal.cn: 在会上说 clarify a point 比说你错了要客气。

definition_zh: n. 清晰，清楚；（思路的）明晰；清澈
definition_en: the quality of being clear and easy to understand, see or think about
core_image: 阳光透过毫无杂质的水面，一眼见底
scene: 老师讲得十分清楚，学生们一下子就明白了。The teacher explained with such clarity that every student understood at once.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clarity 指表达的清晰；句意是老师讲得十分清楚，学生们一下子就明白了。

senses.title: Clearness of expression
senses.definition: the quality of being easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 易于理解的性质
senses.example: Her writing is praised for its clarity.

senses.why: Latin clarus means bright and clear.

senses.title: Clearness of thought

definition_zh: 冲突；抵触；（颜色、日程）不协调；撞击声
definition_en: to fight or disagree strongly, to look wrong together or happen at the same time, or a loud noise of metal hitting metal
core_image: 两面金属盾牌在半空相撞，火星四溅
scene: 两个人站在走廊两头，谁也不肯让路。Their views clash whenever the budget comes up.
sceneCN: 这里 clash 指「冲突；抵触」（第 1 个义项：意见或利益尖锐对立）；句意是每次谈到预算，他们的看法就冲突。

senses.title: A fight or strong disagreement
senses.definition: a short fight or a sharp disagreement between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体之间的短暂打斗或尖锐分歧
senses.example: A clash broke out between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 两个群体之间爆发了冲突。
senses.why: The sound of weapons meeting became the name of the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 兵器相击的声音，变成了这场相遇本身的名称。

senses.title: A bad match in time or colour
senses.definition: to look wrong together, or to be fixed for the same time as something else
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起显得不协调，或与另一事排在同一时间
senses.example: My lecture clashes with the football final.
senses.exampleCN: 我的讲座和足球决赛撞时间了。
senses.why: Two things that cannot sit together are said to strike each other, like metal on metal.
senses.whyCN: 无法并存的两件事被说成互相撞击，就像金属碰金属。

senses.title: A loud metallic noise
senses.definition: a hard, ringing sound made when metal objects hit each other
senses.definitionCN: 金属物件相撞时发出的刺耳响声
senses.example: The clash of the gates echoed down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 铁门的撞击声在街上传开。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the word began as an imitation of that noise.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个词最初就是模仿那种响声。
